newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Koreans hold anti-U.S. rally over alleged murder.
newsitem.headline: S.Koreans hold anti-U.S. rally over alleged murder.

text.p: About 200 protesters demonstrated outside a U.S. military base in South Korea on Friday after a funeral ceremony for a prostitute alleged to have been murdered by an American serviceman, witnesses said.
"We demand a public apology for continuous human rights violation," read a banner held aloft by a demonstrator outside the base in Seoul.

Private Eric Munnich, from Chicago, has been charged with killing Lee Ki-sun on September 7. The body of the 44-year-old woman, who was buried on Friday, was found in a boarding house near a U.S. military base north of Seoul where Munnich was stationed.
Hundreds of riot police were posted outside the military base to prevent trouble.

Lee's death has sparked new calls for a revision of the Status of Forces Agreement (SOFA) governing the 37,000 U.S. troops in South Korea, which remains technically at war with North Korea after the 1950-53 Korean War ended with a ceasefire rather than a peace pact.
The Seoul District Prosecutors' Office on Friday demanded the U.S. Army transfer custody of Munnich to South Korean authorities.
The SOFA agreement calls only for "sympathetic consideration" of such a request, a clause that causes resentment among some South Koreans who say it puts U.S. troops beyond the reach of Korean law.
The U.S. military says Munnich, now detained at a U.S. military installation, admitted to the murder during joint questioning by South Korean police and U.S. military investigators.
The commander of U.S. forces in South Korea, General John Tillely, has described the murder as "tragic and nonsensical".
